- When sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00), model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- After a recent spike (e.g., >73.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend (e.g., >3% drop in 3–5 days), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match observed drop.
- Mean reversion patterns (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70.0) trigger model overconfidence; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until trend stabilizes.
- Sentiment >0.33 (positive) correlates with model overestimating; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days following positive sentiment.
- Sentiment <0.00 (negative) often leads to model underestimating; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 3–5 days following negative sentiment.
- If model forecast >75.0 and true outcome <72.0, apply “cap correction” — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 7 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
